- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.10) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior 30d mean.
- After a recent price spike (e.g., >75.0), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast at +2% above peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (0.00–0.20), model frequently overpredicts; apply 1–2% downward adjustment to avoid mean reversion bias.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is positive (≥ 0.20) and recent price is falling; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to reflect sentiment-driven rebound.
- Forecast horizon 30d often exhibits lag: true price typically dips 1–3 days after model peak; shift forecast down 1–2% for next 3–5 days if sentiment is flat or negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to drift upward; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.0% to prevent overfitting to recent noise.
